paper.title_en: $\Lambda$ Polarization in Weak-Boson-Tagged Jets as a Probe of Longitudinal Spin Transfer and Jet Quenching
paper.abstract_en: Weak-boson-tagged jets produced in unpolarized hadronic collisions are naturally longitudinally polarized owing to the chiral structure of electroweak couplings in the underlying hard partonic scattering. They therefore provide a clean and well-controlled probe of longitudinal spin transfer in hadronization, while also enabling studies of jet quenching in heavy-ion collisions using polarization as a key observable. Within collinear factorization, we present predictions for the longitudinal polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons in $Z^0/W^\pm+\mathrm{jet}$ production in $pp$ and $AA$ collisions. We show that this observable has strong discriminating power among different flavor scenarios of the spin-transfer fragmentation function $G_{1L}$ and is also highly sensitive to jet energy loss in the QGP.
